uncited: Brick-based Hierarchical Storage organizes volumetric data into fixed-size, non-overlapping cubic blocks (bricks) to optimize memory locality, enable efficient sparse access, and support multi-resolution rendering.
**Redundancy Exploitation:** The core principle is to identify and eliminate redundancy in the volumetric data.
**Transformation/Encoding:** Data is transformed into a domain where redundancy is more apparent or compact.
**Quantization (Lossy):** For lossy compression, continuous or high-precision values are mapped to a discrete set of representatives.
Brick-based storage concepts originated in the context of 3D texture caching and volume rendering optimization.

The approach has since been generalized to handle adaptive mesh refinement (ExaBricks), sparse voxel datasets (Sparse Page Table), and semantic segmentation volumes (CSV), reflecting a broader industry shift towards block-based data structures for efficient GPU rendering [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md, 2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md, 4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md].
